title: Trump Hands Victories to Putin, Who Offers More War in Return
partialText: Russia has reaped a diesel deal and an increase in U.S. pressure on Ukraine as President Trump’s political needs align with his longstanding inclinations toward Russia.

title: U.K. and Europe Recoil From Trump’s Diesel Deal With Putin
partialText: Shocked by the U.S. agreement with Russia, which Ukraine has called “a gift” to President Putin, officials in Europe have coalesced around a cautious diplomatic message.

title: Kimberly Guilfoyle Resigns as Ambassador to Greece
partialText: Ms. Guilfoyle was asked to quit by the White House after a string of damaging reports, including that she had asked a Republican donor to pay off a credit card.

title: Pope Leo Has Lung Cancer, Vatican Says
partialText: The surgeons removed the lower lobe of the pope’s right lung after finding a cancerous nodule.

title: Cornell Bans Fraternity Parties and Adds Sexual Assault Investigators
partialText: The expansive changes to campus life, including working closely with the state police, come in the wake of the national uproar caused by allegations of a gang rape at a fraternity house.

title: There’s Worlds Out There More Habitable Than Earth
partialText: Scientists believe there are planets outside our solar system where life is even more abundant and sustainable.

title: Top G.O.P. Groups Pull Support From First House Incumbents
partialText: Two major Republican super PACs are said to be withdrawing cash from the races of the incumbent Representatives Thomas H. Kean Jr. of New Jersey and Mariannette Miller-Meeks of Iowa in an effort to triage the midterm map.

title: Tupac Shakur Murder Conviction Lands Man 40 Years to Life in Prison
partialText: Duane Keith Davis was convicted by a jury of obtaining a gun and pursuing the rapper in a violent act of revenge in 1996.

title: F.B.I. Disrupts Pyongyang Revenue Stream: North Koreans in U.S. Tech Jobs
partialText: F.B.I. investigators worked with the cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike to dismantle so-called laptop farms that steal American identities to earn cash for Pyongyang.

title: A Father’s Mission Is to Show the World ‘What Russia Did to My Family’
partialText: After a glide bomb killed his wife and younger daughter, Yevhen Ovcharov was determined to prevent other Ukrainians from dying the same way.

title: War Collides With Saudi Ambition at a Gathering of Oil Powers
partialText: The tone of the WPC Energy Congress in Riyadh this week was defiant even as delegates were forced to redirect travel or address the audience from afar.

title: Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis Trade Threats to Hit Oil Facilities
partialText: The Iran-backed militia threatened to attack the Saudi energy giant Aramco after the Saudi authorities issued an evacuation notice for an oil facility in the Yemeni capital.

title: Police Identify 42-Year Old Man Killed at Six Flags Over Georgia
partialText: The police identified the 42-year-old man who died at Six Flags Over Georgia on Monday. The company said it was temporarily closing multiple rides in the U.S. and Canada as a precaution.

title: We Know How to Fix Homelessness. Why Don’t More Cities Do It?
partialText: It takes doing things conservatives and progressives both dislike.

title: Martin Shkreli Violated Lifetime Ban From Drug Industry, U.S. Says
partialText: The attorneys general of New York and six other states joined the Federal Trade Commission in accusing the disgraced former pharmaceutical executive of repeatedly violating the ban.
